features.name: redraft_before_refute_any
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment restate the OP's viewpoint in a more nuanced form and then go on to refute it in that same comment?
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; parse it) and, for interpreting the OP viewpoint being restated, title and argument. Return 1 if at least one single comment (a) rewrites/reformulates the OP's viewpoint in the commenter's own words from a more nuanced, qualified or refined perspective (not a mere verbatim quote or a bare summary) AND (b) then refutes or argues against that reformulated or original view, within that same comment. Both parts must occur in one comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Return 0 if no comment does so. Empty comment list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Ignore OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and any reports of the outcome as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is eligible. Quotations of the OP alone do not count as redrafting. Comment order carries no chronology.

h0: redraft_before_refute_any has no association with view change (delta).
h1: Discussions with redraft_before_refute_any = 1 have higher view change (delta) than those with 0.
note: Operationalized as any single comment that both nuance-reframes the OP's view and refutes it. "Nuanced perspective" is judged by the LLM without a fixed scale. OC_comments may contain outcome-related text; the prompt excludes it. Association only; comment timing and reply links unknown.
